title: Thematic Reviews and Industry Findings
summary: How supervisors run thematic reviews, what they mean for firms in and outside the sample, and how to use published findings to strengthen the firm's own controls.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How supervisors run thematic reviews, what they mean for firms in and outside the sample, and how to use published findings to strengthen the firm's own controls.
Learning Objectives: Explain how thematic reviews are scoped and run
Respond effectively when selected for a thematic review
Apply published thematic findings to the firm
Syllabus: Responding to questionnaires, visits and feedback
Reading industry reports: complying with intent, not just wording
Workshop: a gap analysis against a thematic report
Intended Audience: Board members and senior managers accountable for responding to supervisory findings
Compliance, risk and internal audit staff who coordinate remediation and track actions
Project and change managers who deliver remediation programmes
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of supervisory engagement or remediation work is helpful. No prior training is required.
Core Reading: IMF, Good Supervision: Lessons from the Field (Working Paper WP/23/181, 2023)
FSB, Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors (2018)
IOSCO, Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation (2017)
